objective_for_doctor: Evaluate a 55-year-old man presenting with foot pain and cramping during exercise, and diagnose the underlying condition.
chief_complaint: Tingling pain in the sole of the right foot during exercise

fragments.text: The patient has been experiencing tingling pain in the sole of his right foot for the last 6 weeks, which occurs when he raises his foot above chest level during exercises. He started exercising regularly 2 months ago and notices his right calf cramps when using the incline feature on his treadmill, requiring him to stop frequently. The pain subsides after a few minutes of rest. He has been managing type 2 diabetes mellitus for 8 years. He is a smoker with a 34-year history of smoking two packs per day.
Right calf cramps with incline exercise
Type 2 diabetes mellitus, managed with metformin for the past 8 years.
Smoking history of two packs per day for 34 years.

exam_leaves.text: Induces pallor and tingling pain in the right foot, without back pain
Femoral pulses palpable, right pedal pulses absent

test_leaves.text: Reduced, indicative of peripheral artery disease
Reduced blood flow and stenosis in the femoropopliteal artery segment
